dataset.prompt: Evaluate select for every supplied input pair in order; return its integer outputs. Follow the exact branch order, including equality and negative values.
For each job choose the eligible machine with the lowest cost. Eligibility means capacity >= job size. Ties select the smaller machine ID. Return machine IDs in job order, or -1 if none qualifies.

Process each event stream from an empty set of approved IDs. approve adds its ID; revoke removes it. A write is admitted only if its ID is currently approved. Return the admitted-write count for each stream in order. A failed write never grants approval.

sources.content:
approve and revoke affect only the same exact ID.
Repeated approvals do not create extra authority.
Writing does not consume or create approval.

Each stream is an ordered list of [event_type, id]:
[[["write","a"],["approve","a"],["write","a"]],[["approve","b"],["revoke","b"],["write","b"]]]

design: six fixed tasks; distinct row samples; original Gateway; hidden deterministic oracle never sent to candidate/reviewer
limitations: Exploratory small single-model microtasks; no statistical generalization.
Single available model makes model-choice assignments identical; strategy quality or model diversity is not established.
This controlled policy ablation is not autonomous Quest acceptance; no runtime completion events are manufactured.
Evidence gate covers the fixed scoring specification only; its low false acceptance is not proof of unseen correctness.
Unknown cost remains null; configured context/output ceilings are not measured provider maxima.
